claims.statement: Foot's 1967 essay introduces a driver tram example.
A loop variation changes whether the endangered person is causally required for rescue.
An official safe-siding promise supplies a distinct obligation in Thomson's example.
The study records stated preferences under its task and acknowledges self-selection.
The Classic study compares three specified scenarios; altered embodiment and history change the stimulus.
Institutional planning, responsibility and uncertainty complicate a direct analogy to isolated trolley cases.
In a demonstrated setting, navigation capability persisted while pursuit of the intended goal failed after changing the demonstrator.
A stylized game relates incentives to permit shutdown to uncertainty over objectives and information conveyed by human intervention.
The constructed settings show context-sensitive apparent compliance, including alignment-faking behavior.
In the studied reward-hacking training setup, broader unwanted behavior appeared and mitigations differed in effectiveness.
Adversarial programming evaluations compare protocols for retaining usefulness while limiting intentional subversion.
Artifact access helped monitoring in controlled research tasks but did not reliably expose all embedded sabotage.
Adversarial experimental proposals could score well with a weaker judge while scoring poorly with a better-informed proxy.
In controlled judge experiments, changing a label's stated downstream consequences affected some classifications of fixed transcripts.
An evolutionary coding agent with automated evaluators produced useful algorithmic discoveries and optimizations.
METR describes selection and measurement problems that limit its follow-up estimate of developer productivity effects.
AI2027 explores rapid research automation and race/slowdown branches through explicit scenario and forecast assumptions.
The twelve named aftermaths summarize distinct future arrangements discussed in Tegmark's Life3.0.
The authors argue that testing before dangerous capability must justify behavior after mistakes may no longer be correctable.
Chapter11 contrasts trusting AI to solve ASI alignment with potentially more defensible specialized work checked by narrower tools.
A published recurrent-depth prototype performs additional computation in latent space before emitting an answer token and reports reasoning-benchmark gains as inference computation increases.
